answer_plain: In a crop-salt formula fitted to one field trial (not the twin), alfalfa from bacterium-coated seeds reaches about 92 % of normal yield (89 to 93 %) in 7.81 dS/m water, versus about 80 % (78 to 81 %) without the bacterium. Other ways of estimating how salt builds up in the root zone give very different answers, from about 33 % to about 101 % with the bacterium, so this figure depends strongly on that choice.
answer_science: Central estimate under Model C (calibrated to Jizan field trial fresh weight): 91.52 % of normal yield (rounded headline: 92 %, joint 5–95 % interval [88.74, 93.1] %), corresponding to relative_yield_alfalfa_sa187 = 0.9152 fraction (median 0.911 fraction, 50 % IQR [0.9012, 0.9199] fraction, joint 5–95 % interval [0.8874, 0.931] fraction), versus uninoculated relative_yield_alfalfa = 0.7958 fraction (median 0.7946 fraction, 50 % IQR [0.7881, 0.8005] fraction, joint 5–95 % interval [0.7776, 0.808] fraction) (mode = variance, refusal fraction = 0.0 %, max level refusal across question = 0.0 %). Across root-zone salinity closures at 7.81 dS/m (all external crop-salt formulas, not soil-twin outputs, with 0.0 % refusal across all yield series): Model A (FAO-29 fixed leaching) gives inoculated n/a fraction vs uninoculated 0.927 fraction (median 0.9242 fraction, 50 % IQR [0.8973, 0.9481] fraction, joint 5–95 % interval [0.8602, 0.9789] fraction); Model B (twin bucket salt balance) gives inoculated n/a fraction vs uninoculated 1 fraction (median 1 fraction, 50 % IQR [1, 1] fraction, joint 5–95 % interval [1, 1] fraction). Top two Sobol' contributors to output variance: sa187_mock_ratio_fresh (ST = 0.51 [0.46, 0.57], S1 = 0.38) and sa187_benefit_b (ST = 0.36 [0.33, 0.40], S1 = 0.35). Status share of variance: verified_in_source ST = 0.96 (S1 = 0.77), modeller_assumption ST = 0.00 (S1 = 0.00), source_not_checked ST = 0.00 (S1 = 0.00) (joint group total indices can sum to more than 1 because of interactions). Limits: The parameter-uncertainty interval quantifies joint variation over literature constants and twin process parameters only and excludes external-model and twin model-structure error.

headline_plain: In a crop-salt formula fitted to one field trial, alfalfa from bacterium-coated seeds reaches about 92 % of normal yield in 7.81 dS/m water (versus 80 % without it), though other root-zone salt formulas give 33 to 101 %.
headline_science: Central inoculated yield (Model C, trial-calibrated fresh-weight closure) = 91.52 % of normal yield (rounded: 92 %, median 91.1 %, joint 5–95 % interval [88.74, 93.1] %; relative_yield_alfalfa_sa187 = 0.9152 fraction (median 0.911 fraction, 50 % IQR [0.9012, 0.9199] fraction, joint 5–95 % interval [0.8874, 0.931] fraction), mode = variance, refusal = 0.0 %).
limits_plain: The range shows how much the answer moves when uncertain numbers in the models are varied; the models themselves could also be wrong. Crop yields and the bacterial boost come from published crop-salt formulas and one desert farm field trial, not from the soil twin itself.
limits_science: The parameter-uncertainty interval quantifies joint variation over literature constants and twin process parameters only and excludes external-model and twin model-structure error. Multiplies external Maas-Hoffman relative yield by an empirical SA187 field multiplier calibrated to fresh weight at one trial; root-zone EC_e depends strongly on the chosen leaching/accumulation closure (models A, B, C).

admissibility.scope: Joint parameter and literature-constant uncertainty only; excludes model-structure error.
